title: TOEFL iBT
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public TOEFL iBT test specifications. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation in a campus dining services office. The student says, "I was charged twice for the same meal plan transaction on Tuesday, and my account balance is now negative." The employee replies, "I see the duplicate here in the system. I can reverse the second charge today, and it will show up in two business days." What will the employee do?
options: Reverse the duplicate charge so the student is refunded within two business days
Transfer the student to a different meal plan for the rest of the semester
Ask the student to write a formal letter to the finance office
Refund the entire meal plan because of the billing error
items.explanation: The employee states that the second charge can be reversed today and that the reversal will appear in two business days, which matches a partial correction of the duplicate charge.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in an environmental science class. The professor explains that a wetland acts like a sponge, absorbing floodwater slowly and releasing it gradually, and adds that when developers drain wetlands for housing, nearby towns often see higher flood peaks after storms. What is the main function of wetlands as described in the lecture?
options: Generating hydroelectric power for surrounding communities
Absorbing and slowly releasing floodwater to reduce flood peaks
Providing nesting grounds for commercially farmed fish
Filtering salt out of ocean water for drinking
items.explanation: The professor's sponge analogy describes absorption and gradual release of water, and the contrast with drained developments shows flood reduction as the central function.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation between a student and a biology teaching assistant. The student says, "I measured enzyme activity at three temperatures, but the results at the highest temperature were all near zero." The TA responds, "That makes sense, because the enzyme probably denatured. Just report the pattern and explain the denaturation in your discussion section." What does the TA advise the student to do?
options: Repeat the experiment only at the lowest temperature
Discard the high-temperature data as an experimental failure
Report the pattern and attribute the low results to denaturation
Change the lab topic to a different enzyme entirely
items.explanation: The TA accepts the near-zero results as expected behavior and tells the student to report the pattern while explaining denaturation, rather than discarding or repeating anything.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in an art history class. The professor says that Gothic cathedral builders replaced heavy Romanesque walls with ribbed vaults and flying buttresses, which channeled the roof's weight outward and allowed much taller walls filled with stained glass. The professor then asks, "So what made the windows possible?" What does the professor imply made the large windows possible?
options: The invention of clearer glass-making techniques in Rome
A decrease in the overall height of cathedral buildings
Thicker walls that could hold window frames securely
Structural supports that redirected weight away from the walls
items.explanation: The lecture links ribbed vaults and flying buttresses, which redirect weight outward, to taller walls that could hold large stained-glass windows.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation in a university library. The student asks about reserving a group study room for a class project, and the librarian explains that rooms may be booked up to one week in advance through the library website, that bookings expire fifteen minutes after the start time if no one arrives, and that groups larger than six must use the seminar room on the second floor. When does a reservation expire?
options: Fifteen minutes after the scheduled start if the group has not arrived
At the end of the day on which it was made
Immediately if the group has more than six members
One week after it is booked
items.explanation: The librarian states plainly that bookings expire fifteen minutes after the starting time when no group has arrived, which is the condition asked about.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in an astronomy class. The professor describes how Io, one of Jupiter's moons, has intense volcanic activity because tidal forces from Jupiter and the gravitational pulls of neighboring moons flex Io's interior and generate heat. The professor then contrasts Io with our Moon, which lacks such heating. What role do Jupiter and the neighboring moons play for Io?
options: They provide light that warms Io's surface evenly
They exert tidal forces that flex Io's interior and generate heat
They pull Io into orbits that steadily shrink over time
They shield Io from collisions with asteroids
items.explanation: The lecture attributes Io's volcanism to tidal flexing caused by Jupiter and nearby moons, which heats the interior rather than warming the surface from outside.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in a psychology class. The professor describes a study in which one group of students was told a task was enjoyable while another group was paid to do the same task. Later, without payment, the paid group chose to do the task less often than the group that had only been told it was enjoyable. What does the professor use this study to illustrate?
options: That students perform better when they are observed
That enjoyable tasks require no practice to master
That external rewards can weaken intrinsic interest in an activity
That money always increases motivation for simple tasks
items.explanation: The paid group's later reduced interest, compared with the unpaid group that merely heard the task was enjoyable, supports the point that external rewards can undercut intrinsic motivation.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation between a student and a campus housing officer. The student wants to break a dorm lease early because of a family emergency, and the officer explains that early release requires written documentation and approval from the housing director, and that approved releases typically take up to ten days to process. What must the student do to be released from the lease?
options: Move out immediately and notify the housing office by phone
Pay the remaining rent in full at the time of the request
Find another student to take over the room before leaving
Submit written documentation and obtain the housing director's approval
items.explanation: The officer requires both written documentation and the director's approval before an early release can be granted, so the other options skip a required step.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in a geology class. The professor explains that most of Earth's limestone formed in shallow, warm seas where tiny marine organisms secreted calcium carbonate shells, and that after the organisms died the shells accumulated on the sea floor and hardened into rock. The professor then asks why limestone is rarely found on the deep ocean floor. What is the most likely answer implied in the lecture?
options: Most carbonate shells dissolve in deep water before accumulating
Deep ocean water is too cold for calcium carbonate to harden
Strong currents sweep shells off the deep ocean floor
Deep sea sediments are too coarse to mix with carbonate
items.explanation: Since the lecture ties limestone to shallow warm seas and notes its absence in deep water, the implied reason is that carbonate material does not survive at deep-sea depths.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation between a student and a professor about a term paper. The student says the draft focuses on two novels, but the professor responds that the assignment allows only one primary text plus at most three scholarly articles, and suggests cutting the second novel and adding a critical article instead. What change does the professor recommend?
options: Submit the draft as it is because the scope is acceptable
Replace the second novel with one scholarly article
Write about both novels and drop the scholarly sources
Expand the paper to cover three novels in depth
items.explanation: The professor limits the assignment to one primary text plus articles and specifically suggests removing the second novel and adding a critical article in its place.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in an economics class. The professor explains that when a city imposes a tax on plastic bags, stores typically pass the cost to shoppers, and studies of several cities show that bag usage falls sharply in the first year but then levels off as some shoppers simply pay the fee. How does the professor characterize the long-run effect of the bag tax?
options: It increases bag use because of higher production subsidies
It permanently eliminates plastic bag use in every shopping trip
It produces a large initial drop followed by a leveling off
It has no measurable effect on consumer behavior at all
items.explanation: The professor describes a sharp first-year decline and then a plateau once some shoppers begin paying the fee, which matches a large initial drop followed by leveling off.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation in a student services office. The adviser explains that international students may work on campus up to twenty hours per week during the academic term and full time during official breaks, but only in jobs directly administered by the university. What restriction does the adviser emphasize?
options: Students may work only twenty hours total for the whole term
Students may work off campus with a simple written notice
Students may not work during official university breaks
Students may hold only positions run by the university itself
items.explanation: The adviser limits employment to jobs directly administered by the university, which is the specific restriction the question asks about.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in a music history class. The professor notes that baroque concertos typically alternate between the full ensemble, called the ripieno, and a small group of soloists, known as the concertino, and that this contrast creates the echo effects heard in many works of the period. What musical effect does the alternation between these groups produce?
options: Echo-like contrasts between the full ensemble and soloists
A continuous loud volume throughout the movement
A gradual slowing of tempo at the end of each section
Complete silence between every melodic phrase
items.explanation: The professor explicitly connects the alternation of ripieno and concertino with the echo effects characteristic of baroque concertos.

items.stem: Listen to part of a conversation between a student and a campus recreation employee. The student wants to join the indoor rock climbing club but has missed the registration window, and the employee says a waitlist exists, that people usually drop off within a week of the semester starting, and that the student should check the online portal each morning for openings. What does the employee suggest?
options: Take a different outdoor adventure course instead
Check the portal daily in case waitlisted climbers drop out
Speak with the club president to bypass the waitlist
Register again when the next semester begins
items.explanation: The employee points the student to the daily-updated online portal as the way to catch openings created when others drop from the waitlist.

items.stem: Listen to part of a lecture in a botany class. The professor explains that some plants close their stomata during the hottest part of the day to conserve water, which also blocks carbon dioxide intake and temporarily slows photosynthesis, and that these plants often fix carbon dioxide at night instead. Why do the plants described take up carbon dioxide at night?
options: Nighttime temperatures increase the rate of photosynthesis directly
Carbon dioxide is more abundant during daylight hours
Open stomata at night allow carbon uptake while water loss is limited
Photosynthesis can only occur in complete darkness
items.explanation: Because daytime stomata closure prevents gas exchange, the plants open stomata at night to absorb carbon dioxide while losing less water in cooler air.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Seed banks store seeds from thousands of plant species in freezers so that future growers can replant crops or restore damaged ecosystems. Because seeds of most crop plants survive freezing for decades, a single properly maintained facility can preserve genetic diversity far longer than any individual farm." According to the passage, why can one facility preserve diversity for so long?
options: Freezers consume less energy than fields of growing plants
Genetic diversity changes very little over short periods
Farms are unable to store seeds at all in modern agriculture
Most crop seeds remain viable when frozen for decades
items.explanation: The passage attributes the long preservation window directly to the fact that most crop seeds survive freezing for decades under proper maintenance.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Medieval trade fairs were not merely marketplaces; they were legal spaces where travelling merchants could sign contracts under the protection of local lords, resolve disputes through specialized courts, and exchange currency at rates posted publicly." As used in the passage, what does the word "protected" most nearly mean?
options: Defended and guaranteed safe by authority
Recorded in written ledgers
Concealed from view
Charged a fee for service
items.explanation: In context the lords guarantee the safety and legality of the merchants' activities, so defended and guaranteed safe is the intended meaning.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Archaeologists studying a coastal settlement found fish bones far outnumbering the bones of land animals. Analysis of the artifacts showed sophisticated net weights and harpoon points. Together these findings suggest that the community depended heavily on fishing rather than on hunting." Which of the following best supports the conclusion in the final sentence?
options: A few land animal bones were discovered near the settlement entrance
Fish bones greatly outnumbered land animal bones and fishing tools were found
The climate of the region supported both forests and open water
The settlement was located several days' walk from the coast
items.explanation: The ratio of fish to land animal bones combined with net weights and harpoons is the direct evidence cited for heavy reliance on fishing.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Unlike steam engines, which burn fuel continuously, electric motors draw power only when under load, so a factory that shifts heavy machinery to off-peak hours can reduce both its energy bill and its strain on the regional grid." It can be inferred from the passage that off-peak scheduling benefits factories mainly because it
options: Increases the total output of the factory
Allows motors to run at higher top speeds
Reduces electricity costs and grid demand
Eliminates the need for electric motors
items.explanation: The passage states two outcomes of off-peak scheduling, a lower energy bill and less strain on the grid, which together match the reduction of costs and demand.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Bioluminescent fungi glow because a chemical reaction involving luciferin produces light with very little heat. Researchers believe the glow attracts insects that then carry the fungi's spores to new logs, though some argue the light simply is a byproduct of metabolism." What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Insects can see wavelengths of light that humans cannot detect
Luciferin is used commercially in medical imaging laboratories
All glowing organisms produce light through the same chemical pathway
Fungal bioluminescence may serve to attract spore-dispersing insects, though its purpose is debated
items.explanation: The passage presents the insect-attraction hypothesis and then a competing byproduct explanation, so the main idea is the debated function of the glow.

items.stem: Read the passage. "The collapse of the Western Roman Empire did not end urban life everywhere. Cities along the eastern Mediterranean, notably Constantinople, maintained forums, aqueducts, and codified laws for centuries after western cities had shrunk." The passage contrasts eastern cities with western cities in order to
options: Emphasize that urban continuity varied greatly by region
Prove that Constantinople was larger than Rome at its peak
Show that aqueducts were unknown in the western provinces
Argue that law codes were less important than markets
items.explanation: By noting continued urban infrastructure in the east after western decline, the author highlights regional variation in how long urban life persisted.

items.stem: Read the passage. "A prairie fire that sweeps through dry grass kills many individual plants but returns nutrients to the soil and clears away dead thatch, making room for new growth. Frequent light fires therefore often benefit the ecosystem more than rare, intense fires that burn deep into the soil." According to the passage, why do frequent light fires benefit the prairie?
options: They prevent all plant species from regenerating after the fire
They recycle nutrients and remove dead plant material without deep soil damage
They leave the soil so hot that weeds cannot survive
They increase the amount of rainfall the prairie receives each year
items.explanation: The passage credits light fires with returning nutrients and clearing thatch while contrasting them with rare fires that damage soil deeply.

items.stem: Read the passage. "When the telescope replaced the astrolabe for navigation, sailors could determine longitude more reliably, and shipping schedules became predictable enough that insurers began pricing risk with new precision." Which of the following best describes the organization of the passage?
options: It presents a problem, then two competing solutions in order
It compares the designs of two scientific instruments in detail
It gives a technological change and then a practical consequence of that change
It chronicles a famous voyage from departure to return
items.explanation: The passage moves from the adoption of the telescope over the astrolabe to the resulting reliability of longitude and predictable insurance pricing, a cause followed by consequence.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Corals expel the symbiotic algae living in their tissues when water temperatures stay above a critical threshold for several weeks. If cooler conditions return quickly, the algae may repopulate the coral; if the heat stress persists, the coral starves and its white skeleton becomes visible." The word "repopulate" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: measure the density of the tissue
cover the skeleton with sediment
completely destroy the tissue
colonize the tissue once again
items.explanation: In context the algae return and live in the coral tissue again after being expelled, which matches colonize the tissue once again.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Early windmills in Persia turned on a vertical axis and could catch wind from any direction, but they produced little torque. Later European mills used a horizontal axis that faced only one direction yet drove heavy millstones with ease." What advantage did the European design have over the Persian design?
options: It generated greater turning force for heavy work
It could operate regardless of wind direction
It required fewer materials to construct
It was more efficient in very low winds
items.explanation: The European mills produced little torque in the Persian description but drove heavy millstones with ease, indicating greater turning force as the key advantage.

items.stem: Read the passage. "A study followed two groups of city gardeners for five years. Plots managed without synthetic pesticides hosted more insect species and more pollinator visits than plots sprayed on a fixed schedule, yet the marketable yield of vegetables did not differ significantly between the two groups." Which of the following statements about the study is supported?
options: Sprayed plots produced dramatically higher vegetable yields
Unsprayed plots supported more insect diversity without losing yield
Pollinators avoided all gardens located inside the city
Synthetic pesticides increased the number of insect species observed
items.explanation: The unsprayed plots had more insect species and pollinator visits while yields stayed statistically similar, which matches the statement about diversity without yield loss.

items.stem: Read the passage. "The invention of movable type is often credited to Gutenberg around 1450, yet similar experiments with reusable clay and metal characters had appeared in East Asia centuries earlier. What differed in Europe was the combination of an oil-based ink, the screw press, and an alphabet of relatively few letters, which together made mass printing economical." According to the passage, what made mass printing economical in Europe?
options: The availability of free labor in European printing houses
The early invention of paper in Asian workshops
The combination of oil-based ink, the screw press, and a small alphabet
A sudden increase in demand for handwritten manuscripts
items.explanation: The final sentence names oil-based ink, the screw press, and the small alphabet as the combination that made European mass printing economical.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Desert beetles in the Namib Desert collect fog on their banded wing cases; droplets roll toward their mouths along microscopic channels. Engineers studying the beetles have since designed building panels that harvest atmospheric moisture in a similar fashion." The passage primarily serves to
options: Describe the water requirements of desert insects
Explain how fog forms over coastal deserts
Compare beetle species from different continents
Show how a biological adaptation inspired engineering design
items.explanation: The passage links the beetle's fog-harvesting wing pattern to panels engineered after it, making biological inspiration of design the primary purpose.

items.stem: Read the passage. "The treaty was signed in 1920, but historians debate whether it ended the conflict or merely postponed it, since several of its territorial clauses were never enforced and border disputes resurfaced within a decade." According to the passage, why do some historians see the treaty as postponing rather than ending the conflict?
options: Several territorial clauses went unenforced and disputes returned quickly
A second treaty in 1930 replaced the original terms entirely
The treaty was signed after open warfare had already resumed
The signatories refused to establish any border commissions
items.explanation: The unenforced territorial clauses and the return of border disputes within a decade are the stated reasons for viewing the treaty as a postponement.

items.stem: Read the passage. "Honeybee hives maintain an internal temperature near 35 degrees Celsius regardless of the weather outside. On hot days bees fan the comb with their wings and spread water droplets to cool it; on cold days they shiver their flight muscles to generate heat." Which sentence best expresses the essential information of the passage?
options: Bees spread water primarily to communicate with other members of the hive
Honeybee colonies actively regulate hive temperature through behavior, whether it is hot or cold outside
Shivering flight muscles is a behavior limited to winter months
Honeybees can only survive in regions where outdoor temperatures stay mild
items.explanation: The core point is active temperature regulation by fanning and water on hot days and muscle shivering on cold days, which the first option captures completely.

items.stem: You are preparing for an independent speaking task. The prompt asks, "Some students prefer to study alone in a quiet place, while others prefer to study in a group. Which do you prefer and why?" Which of the following responses best fulfills the task requirements?
options: Libraries are quiet and group study rooms are reserved online, so both options exist for students who need them.
Studying is important for students, and there are many places on campus where people study every day of the week.
I prefer studying alone because I can set my own pace, review notes without interruptions, and decide when to take breaks, and I once finished a difficult statistics chapter this way.
My roommate studies in groups and I study alone, and we both have different majors in the same building.
items.explanation: The task asks for a clear preference with supporting reasons, and the first response states a preference, gives specific reasons, and adds a brief example.

items.stem: Listen to a campus announcement. The university will close the east parking lot for resurfacing from Monday through Friday, and permit holders for that lot may park in the west structure at no extra cost during the closure. Now answer. What change to parking will occur next week, and how will permit holders be affected?
options: Both lots will stay open, but only compact cars may use the east lot
Permit holders will receive refunds for the week of construction
The west structure will close, and east lot permit holders must pay higher rates
The east lot will be resurfaced, and permit holders may use the west structure free of charge
items.explanation: The announcement states the east lot closes for resurfacing and that the west structure becomes available to those permit holders at no extra cost.

items.stem: Read a short passage. The campus writing center will move to the library's second floor beginning next semester, and walk-in appointments will still be available, though the hours will shrink from twelve to eight per week. Now answer. What are two changes about the writing center mentioned in the announcement?
options: It will change location and reduce its weekly walk-in hours
It will change location and stop accepting walk-in students
It will expand hours and charge a small fee for appointments
It will close for the semester and reopen downtown
items.explanation: The announcement names exactly two changes, the move to the library's second floor and the reduction of walk-in hours from twelve to eight per week.

items.stem: Listen to a conversation. A student asks about a biology lab fee, and the coordinator explains that the fee covers disposable safety goggles and reagents, that it is waived for students receiving full tuition grants, and that the waiver is applied automatically once registration is confirmed. Why does the coordinator mention the automatic waiver?
options: To encourage the student to withdraw from the laboratory course
To tell the student that no separate application is needed for the waiver
To explain that the fee will double next academic year
To warn the student that goggles must be purchased elsewhere
items.explanation: Emphasizing that the waiver is applied automatically tells the student that no extra paperwork or separate application is required.

items.stem: Listen to a lecture excerpt. The professor states that honeybees communicate the location of flowers through a waggle dance, that the angle of the dance relative to the hive indicates direction relative to the sun, and that the duration of the waggle encodes distance. What two pieces of information does the dance convey?
options: The sweetness of nectar and the time of day the flowers open
The species of flower and the number of bees already foraging
The direction of flowers relative to the sun and their approximate distance
The temperature outside and the wind speed at the hive
items.explanation: The lecture names direction relative to the sun and distance encoded by waggle duration as the two data points transmitted by the dance.

items.stem: You are preparing an integrated speaking task. A reading passage states that some universities require first-year students to live on campus, and a listening segment has a student arguing that the requirement should be dropped because commuting students save money and many live close enough to benefit from home support. Which response best summarizes the student's position?
options: The student supports the requirement because residence halls build community among new students
The student is unsure about the requirement and wants more data on dorm costs
The student believes only out-of-state students should be required to live on campus
The student opposes the on-campus living requirement because commuting saves money and family support is nearby
items.explanation: The listening segment presents two arguments against the requirement, cost savings and proximity to family, and the first option summarizes both accurately.

items.stem: Listen to a conversation. A student tells the financial aid officer that a required textbook costs eighty dollars more than the estimated allowance in the aid package, and the officer replies that the allowance may be revised with a bookstore receipt and that a temporary book voucher can be issued the same day. What two actions can the student take?
options: Submit a receipt to request an allowance revision and obtain a same-day book voucher
Return the textbook and reapply for financial aid next semester
Borrow the book from the library and drop the course
Pay the difference personally and file no paperwork at all
items.explanation: The officer offers two concrete remedies, a receipt-based allowance revision and an immediate temporary voucher, which the first option lists together.

items.stem: You are answering an independent speaking task. The prompt asks, "Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? Teachers should assign homework every day." Which response best addresses the task?
options: Whether homework is assigned daily depends on the building schedule and the availability of classrooms.
I disagree because daily homework leaves no time for review and extracurricular activities, and students in my chemistry class improved more when assignments came three times a week.
Homework has existed for a very long time in schools around the world, and teachers have many different styles of grading.
My school is large and has many teachers who teach chemistry, biology, and physics during the same week.
items.explanation: The task requires a clear stance plus reasons, and the first response disagrees, gives specific reasons, and supports them with a concrete example.

items.stem: Listen to a lecture excerpt. The professor describes the tragedy of the commons, in which individual herders sharing a public pasture each benefit from adding one more animal, yet overgrazing eventually ruins the pasture for everyone, and notes that towns have responded with grazing quotas or enforced fences. What problem does the professor illustrate?
options: Herders are unable to count the animals in their own flocks
Fences are ineffective at protecting grassland from drought
Shared resources can be depleted when individuals act in their own short-term interest
Private ownership always reduces the productivity of pastureland
items.explanation: The example of each herder adding animals until the pasture fails illustrates depletion of a shared resource driven by individual self-interest.

items.stem: Read a notice. The student government will hold elections two weeks earlier than last year so that results are known before the spring break planning meetings, and candidates must file nomination forms by the end of next week. Now answer. Why are elections being held earlier, and what must candidates do?
options: The registrar's office requested a change, and candidates must attend a debate forum
Budget approval was delayed, and candidates must pay a filing fee
Turnout is expected to be higher before spring break, and candidates must collect fifty signatures
Results will be ready before spring break planning, and candidates must file nominations by the end of next week
items.explanation: The notice gives one purpose, earlier results for spring break planning, and one requirement, nomination forms by the end of next week, which the first option combines.

items.stem: Listen to a conversation. A student asks whether an incomplete grade in a seminar can be converted to a letter grade after graduation, and the instructor replies that the deadline is the last day of the following term, that an extension requires approval from the academic dean, and that incomplete grades older than one year lapse to a failing grade. What happens if the student waits more than a year?
options: The incomplete grade automatically becomes a failing grade
The instructor can extend the deadline without approval
The grade converts to a pass automatically
The student may still graduate without further action
items.explanation: The instructor states that incomplete grades older than one year lapse to a failure, which is the direct consequence of waiting too long.

items.stem: Listen to a lecture excerpt. The professor explains that owls rotate their heads up to two hundred and seventy degrees because their eye sockets are fixed tubes, and describes a network of blood vessels that stores oxygenated blood heading to the brain. What two facts does the professor give to explain the head rotation?
options: Owls have unusually long necks, and their ear openings are asymmetrically placed
Owl eyes are fixed in place, and special blood vessels supply oxygen to the brain during rotation
Owl wings are silent in flight, and their feathers shed water easily
Owls hunt only at night, and their prey cannot see them approaching
items.explanation: The two explanatory facts are the immobile tube-shaped eye sockets and the vascular reservoir that keeps oxygen flowing to the brain while the head turns.

items.stem: You are preparing an independent speaking task. The prompt asks, "Some people prefer to eat at restaurants, and others prefer to cook at home. Which do you prefer?" Which response best fulfills the task?
options: Restaurants serve food and home cooks also serve food, so both options are common in most cities around the world.
My family eats out on Fridays and cooks the rest of the week, and everyone seems to enjoy both kinds of meals.
I prefer cooking at home because I can control ingredients and portion sizes, and it costs less per meal, which helped me budget while working part-time.
Cooking requires pots and pans while restaurants require money, so each has its own requirements.
items.explanation: A strong independent response states a preference with specific supporting reasons and a personal example, which the first option does while the others do not commit to a choice.

items.stem: Listen to a conversation. A student reports a broken dryer in the residence hall laundry room, and the facilities staff member says a technician is scheduled for Thursday, that students may use dryers in the adjacent hall at no charge until repairs finish, and that the student should report any further problems by phone. What solution does the staff member offer in the meantime?
options: Hang all clothing outside regardless of the weather
Wait until Thursday without using any laundry facilities
Buy a personal dryer at a discounted campus rate
Use the dryers in the neighboring hall without paying during the outage
items.explanation: The interim solution named is free use of dryers in the adjacent hall while the technician repairs the broken machine later in the week.

items.stem: Listen to a lecture excerpt. The professor describes coral bleaching as the expulsion of symbiotic algae after heat stress, notes that recovery requires cooler water for several months, and warns that repeated bleaching events leave corals too energy-depleted to recover. What consequence of repeated bleaching does the professor emphasize?
options: Corals lose so much energy that recovery becomes impossible after repeated events
Corals grow twice as fast during periods of cooler water
Algae permanently move to deeper water and never return
Fish populations increase because coral cover expands
items.explanation: The professor's warning is that repeated bleaching exhausts coral energy reserves to the point where recovery can no longer occur.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture, then choose the option that best characterizes how the lecture relates to the passage. The passage argues that city tree-planting programs mainly improve air quality by filtering pollutants. The lecture counters that mature street trees filter only a small fraction of urban pollutants, and that the largest measurable benefits are shade-driven cooling of pavements and buildings. Which statement best summarizes the relationship?
options: The lecture accepts the passage's claim but adds that trees should be planted only in parks
The lecture challenges the passage's emphasis on air quality by arguing that cooling benefits are larger than filtration benefits
The lecture supports the passage completely by providing additional measurements of pollutant filtering
The lecture is unrelated to the passage because it discusses a different city program entirely
items.explanation: The lecture shifts the primary benefit from filtration to shade-driven cooling, which directly challenges the passage's emphasis rather than supporting it.

items.stem: You are writing the integrated essay. The reading states that solar-powered irrigation pumps reduce fuel costs for small farms, and the lecture notes that the pumps only operate during daylight, that cloudy weeks force farmers to ration water, and that battery storage doubles the upfront price. Which point from the lecture most directly qualifies the reading's claim?
options: Solar pumps are heavier than diesel pumps and therefore harder to install
Small farms cannot obtain financing for any new equipment whatsoever
Daylight-only operation and the cost of batteries limit reliability compared with the reading's optimistic picture
Irrigation is unnecessary in regions where crops receive rainfall
items.explanation: The lecture's daylight limitation and battery cost directly temper the reading's claim of straightforward savings, so the first option best qualifies it.

items.stem: You are drafting an academic discussion post. A classmate writes, "Universities should require all first-year students to take a course in statistics, because data interpretation appears in nearly every field." Which response best contributes to the discussion by adding a relevant idea?
options: Statistics is a subject that involves numbers, and numbers appear in many places around the world.
My cousin took statistics last year and said the class was fine, and he is now studying economics.
Universities offer many courses besides statistics, and students have to choose among them each term.
I agree that data skills are broadly useful, but the requirement should be paired with discipline-specific examples so students see how statistics applies to their own major.
items.explanation: A strong discussion post builds on the classmate's claim with a specific, relevant extension, and the first option does so by proposing discipline-specific examples.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture. The passage claims that the invention of the printing press rapidly raised literacy across Europe. The lecture argues that printing capacity grew faster than the supply of trained teachers, that many printed books were expensive relative to daily wages, and that measurable literacy gains came only a century later. Which thesis best captures the lecture's position for an integrated essay?
options: The lecture disputes the passage by showing that book supply outpaced teachers and affordability, delaying real literacy gains
The lecture agrees with the passage but adds that maps were the most printed item
The lecture confirms the press caused immediate literacy growth in every European region
The lecture argues that handwriting remained more accurate than printed text for centuries
items.explanation: The lecture rebuts the passage by identifying teacher shortages and high book prices that pushed literacy gains a century out, which the first thesis captures.

items.stem: You are planning an academic discussion post responding to the prompt, "Should universities limit class sizes in introductory courses?" Which opening sentence best states a clear position with a reason?
options: My introductory biology class had a lot of students, and the professor used slides during most of the lectures.
Yes, introductory classes should cap enrollment because beginners need frequent feedback that large lectures cannot provide.
Universities are large institutions that offer many programs of study across many buildings on campus.
Class sizes vary between departments and even between terms, so the topic is complicated for many reasons.
items.explanation: A discussion post should open with a clear stance plus justification, and the first sentence states support for caps with a concrete reason about feedback.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture. The passage lists three advantages of remote work, including reduced commuting emissions, flexible schedules, and access to a wider talent pool. The lecture counters that home offices often shift energy use to residential buildings, that many remote workers report longer unpaid hours, and that time-zone gaps slow team decisions. Which passage advantage does the lecture most directly undermine?
options: Access to a wider talent pool, by showing that employers hire only locally
All three advantages equally, by providing data supporting each counter-claim
Flexible schedules, by showing that remote workers often end up working longer unpaid hours
Reduced commuting emissions, by arguing that cars emit no greenhouse gases
items.explanation: The claim that remote workers log longer unpaid hours most directly undercuts the flexibility advantage, while the other two lecture points target different advantages.

items.stem: You are writing an integrated essay summary. The reading passage states that museums should return artifacts acquired during colonial rule, and the lecture argues that some source countries lack climate-controlled storage that would protect the objects. Which accurate sentence for the essay body best represents the lecture?
options: The lecturer fully supports the passage by describing successful repatriation ceremonies held last year
The lecturer argues that museums themselves lack storage and therefore should sell the artifacts instead
The lecturer claims that colonial acquisitions were always conducted with proper legal documentation
The lecturer disputes the return of artifacts on the grounds that some source countries cannot yet provide climate-controlled storage
items.explanation: The lecture's objection rests on storage capacity concerns, which the first sentence states accurately without adding claims the lecturer never made.

items.stem: You are preparing an academic discussion response to the prompt, "Is it better for a city to invest in public transit or in new roads?" A classmate argues for roads. Which reply best advances the discussion?
options: New roads can relieve congestion short term, but transit moves more people per lane and tends to cut per-transportation costs for households without cars.
Roads are made of asphalt and transit vehicles are made of metal, so the materials are different in important ways.
I once sat in traffic for two hours, and the experience was unpleasant for everyone in the car that day.
Cities are large and transportation is important, and both roads and transit involve engineering considerations.
items.explanation: The reply acknowledges the classmate's point and counters with specific reasoning about capacity and household costs, which deepens the discussion rather than restating it.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture. The passage describes the reintroduction of wolves to Yellowstone and credits the wolves with reducing elk herds and allowing willow and aspen recovery along rivers. The lecture notes that a severe drought in the same period lowered elk numbers independently and that willow recovery was uneven across the park. How does the lecture qualify the passage?
options: It argues that wolf reintroduction had no measurable effect of any kind in Yellowstone
It suggests that drought and uneven recovery, not wolf predation alone, explain the changes along the rivers
It claims that willows declined because wolves ate them directly
It states that elk populations increased steadily after the wolves arrived
items.explanation: By introducing drought as a confounding factor and uneven recovery as a complication, the lecture qualifies rather than denies the passage's causal story.

items.stem: You are drafting a body paragraph for an integrated essay. The reading says that standardized exams predict university performance, and the lecture says that high school grades predict performance better because they average effort across four years. Which topic sentence best previews a paragraph comparing the two sources?
options: Standardized exams are administered in many countries and high school grades are recorded on transcripts at many schools.
The lecture describes several kinds of exams and the reading lists the names of past university presidents.
While the reading presents standardized exams as strong predictors of performance, the lecture argues that cumulative high school grades reflect sustained effort more reliably.
Both the reading and the lecture agree that predicting university performance is difficult for anyone.
items.explanation: A comparative topic sentence names each source's claim and the axis of contrast, which the first option does by pitting exam prediction against cumulative grade prediction.

items.stem: You are answering an academic discussion prompt that asks, "Should schools teach financial literacy as a required course?" Which response best supports its position with specific reasoning?
options: Some countries require the course and others do not, and the requirements change from year to year.
Money is important and schools teach many subjects, so financial literacy could be one of them in some places.
My bank offers free classes, and the classes cover topics like savings and credit cards for adults.
Yes, because students who learn budgeting and interest calculations early are less likely to accumulate high-interest debt in their first years of independence.
items.explanation: The first option takes a clear position and grounds it in a specific consequence, reduced high-interest debt, while the others remain general or anecdotal.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture. The passage states that banning single-use plastic bags leads consumers to reuse paper and cloth bags. The lecture counters that paper bag production uses more water and energy per bag, that cloth bags must be reused hundreds of times to offset their footprint, and that many bags are still discarded after brief use. Which conclusion best reflects the lecture?
options: The environmental benefit of bag bans is smaller than the passage implies once production impacts and reuse rates are considered
Plastic bags are harmless to wildlife in every environment where they are discarded
Paper bags are always superior to both plastic and cloth alternatives worldwide
Bag bans increased total bag consumption to exactly the levels seen before the bans
items.explanation: The lecture's production-cost and reuse arguments shrink the net benefit claimed by the passage, which is exactly the first conclusion.

items.stem: You are concluding an academic discussion post about whether group projects should count heavily toward final grades. Which sentence best closes the post by restating a position and pointing forward?
options: Group projects exist in many courses and involve collaboration among students who work together for several weeks each term.
Because peer feedback improves the quality of drafts, group projects should count for a substantial share of the grade, provided instructors build in peer evaluations.
Grading is difficult and instructors are busy, and students also have assignments in other courses at the same time.
I have been in both good groups and bad groups, and both types of groups met in the same classroom building.
items.explanation: An effective closing restates the stance and adds a forward-looking condition, which the first sentence does by linking peer feedback to peer evaluation requirements.

items.stem: Read a passage and listen to a lecture. The passage says that remote proctoring software protects exam integrity, and the lecture responds that the software often flags innocent behavior such as looking away to think, that it performs inconsistently for students with older webcams, and that support response times leave some students locked out of exams. Which summary sentence best captures the lecture?
options: The lecture claims that older webcams are more accurate than modern ones for identity checks
The lecture supports remote proctoring by showing how camera checks prevent cheating in large courses
The lecture challenges remote proctoring by citing false flags, inconsistent hardware performance, and slow support that can block exam access
The lecture argues that proctoring software should replace written exams entirely at every university
items.explanation: The first sentence accurately aggregates the lecture's three criticisms without inventing claims the lecturer did not make.

items.stem: You are opening an integrated essay about whether public libraries remain necessary in the age of internet search. The reading says digital access makes libraries obsolete, and the lecture says libraries provide reliable curated sources, free internet access for patrons without home connections, and trained staff who verify information. Which introduction sentence best states a thesis?
options: Libraries are buildings that contain many books, and the internet is a network that connects computers around the world.
Public libraries opened many decades before the internet existed, and they continue to occupy buildings in most cities.
The reading and the lecture both discuss information and both mention that people sometimes look up facts online.
Although the reading claims that the internet has made public libraries unnecessary, the lecture shows that libraries remain vital through curated collections, free access, and expert guidance.
items.explanation: An integrated introduction should preview the contrast between sources, and the first sentence states the reading's claim against the lecture's three supporting points.
